name: A Pelter's Reckoning
description: A skinner's tally scratched on a strip of wolf-hide with a knife point, rolled up and pushed into a crack in the swallet's throat to keep it dry.

name: The Drovers' Tally-Board
description: A board of split oak prised off the pound's gate-post, notched in the drovers' way: a long cut for a score of ewes, a short one for a single beast.

name: Hedda's Kiln-Book
description: A limeburner's day-book, its pages gone stiff and white at the edges with the dust, kept on a nail by the draw-arch of the near kiln.

name: The Table-Warden's Places
description: A long roll of paper wound on a stick, the seating of the Brow's Long Table in the Table-Warden's hand, every household's place and every bell at the foot.

name: Enid Drove's Evening Count
description: A slate hung on a nail inside the wheelhouse door, chalked with two columns of numbers every evening and wiped every morning; this is the one she forgot to wipe.

name: The Southcote Plough-Book
description: A farm book in a calf cover gone green, the terraces drawn in it one to a page; it was lying open on the top terrace wall, weighed down with a flint.

name: The Briarfoot Tally
description: The Wardens' tally-board from the foot of Briarfoot Watch, chalked in two hands and a third; a copy on paper is taken to the Rest every season, and this is the copy.

name: Scions and Stocks
description: A grafter's notebook with slips of bark pressed between its pages, each labelled with the farm it went to and whether it took.

name: The Scouring Song
description: The walking-song the scourers sing round the outline of the Chalk Hound, written out on the back of a wheelwright's bill and pinned inside the lodge door so the children learn the order of the verses.

name: The Listener's Book
description: The Wardens' book of verses heard on the Brow, this year's pages; three pages are headed and left blank.

name: Bel Axtree's List
description: A list of names written on the back of a waybill and kept in a tin under the first wheel, with the dates the carters were buried beside them.

name: The Road Crew's Pay-Book
description: A pay-book in covers of oak board, older than any book in the Vale that is not the Roll, every name in it written once and none struck out.

name: The Kennel Book
description: The Wardens' kennel book, the pack's names and lines written up by the kennel-master; the last page is three nights old.

name: The Unstruck Name-Board
description: A new name-board from the Struck Gibbet, the paint still sharp, the name on it whole; the stroke through it has not been painted.

name: The Pit-Reckoning
description: A tally-stick as long as an arm, notched by every farm on the down each Long Table when its sack goes down the kept pit; it hangs from the windlass on a thong.

name: What Rookdown Told the Bees
description: A bee-keeper's book of the news told to the skeps, one line each, kept dry in the niche by the garth gate.

name: The Ash Watch Log
description: The keepers' log-book at Ash Watch, handed from keeper to keeper every ninth day with the beacon's flint and steel.

name: The Hound Watch Log
description: The log-book at Hound Watch, its pages ringed where the keeper's mug stood on them.

name: The Beacon-Keeper's Reckoning
description: A reckoning of wood and nights kept by the keeper of the Brow Beacon, with the four burnings of a hundred years copied in the front, and this spring's two after them.

name: A Shepherd's Knot
description: A length of greased cord tied in a Fallowfold counting-knot, jammed in a gap in the Holt's flint wall; the knots read like a sentence to anyone raised on the West Downs.

name: A Child's Slate
description: A child's writing slate left in the grass between the Hushwatch stones, a name chalked on it in big careful capitals.

name: A Woodfolk Cutting-Tally
description: A Woodfolk fletcher's tally-stick from the Grey End, notched for every grey thorn cut, with a line of cramped Valish burned along it.

name: The Fire-Keepers' Rota
description: A board of Rookdown households, each with its night to keep the fire at the Cliff Hearth, the names painted and repainted until the board is thick as a door.

name: A Carved Lintel-Stone
description: A lintel-stone fallen from the door of the hut at Lamb's Bottom, carved along its underside where only a person lying in the doorway would read it.

name: The Sheepwash Tally
description: A wash-tally cut in a board and hung on the sheep-gate of the Old Sheepwash, a notch for every flock put through, with a note tied to it.

name: The Hayward's Pound-Book
description: The pound-book of the Pinfold, every stray penned and every penny paid, kept in a box nailed inside the gate where the bell hangs.

name: A Carter's Rain-Count
description: A carter's reckoning of crossings at the Larkbourne Ford and how many times the bell rang under the water, pushed into the joint of the parapet.

name: A Scratched Slate
description: A flake of slate scratched with a nail, found in the wet at the foot of the Whitecut Falls where the spray caves drain.

name: A Pilgrim's Note
description: A note tucked under the pilgrims' bench at the Last Look, folded small, addressed to nobody.

name: A Grave-Keeper's Note
description: A note folded into a gap behind the headstone at the Cliff Graves that turned in the night to face inland, weighted with a shell.

name: Aldous Hounder's Cord
description: A scourer's white cord, the kind the Hounders tie on their lodge gate after every scouring, knotted round a rake-head worn to a stub. It ran from the swallet's throat to the bottom, and it was taut.

name: The Old Hound's Tooth
description: A wolf's tooth as long as a hand, white as scoured chalk and faintly warm. Hounders' children used to be told the Chalk Hound had teeth like this; none of them believed it.

name: The Hurdwell Bell
description: A small bronze family bell, green with the ground it was buried in, the name HURDWELL cut round its shoulder and the date of the family's first Long Table under it. It rings a little flat, as the Toll's cousins do.

name: A Sack of Lime Bay Quicklime
description: A double sack of quicklime from the Lime Bay Kilns, tied at the neck with Hedda's red cord so the Ashways know it is theirs. It is warm through the sacking and it must be kept out of the rain.

name: A Hound-Couple
description: A pair of brass-ringed collars joined by a short chain, the Wardens' kennel-mark on each ring. Two hounds run coupled so the young one learns from the old. The collars are unbuckled, not broken.

name: Bellmouth's Collar
description: The lead hound's collar, with the little bell the Wardens hang on the lead hound so the pack can hear where she is. The bell has been stopped with a twist of grass.

name: A Verse-Slate from the Hush Steps
description: A slate left on the last of the Hush Steps by the Listener before this one, with a verse chalked on it: 'Down the steps and the steps go down, / and the last step is the one we found.'

name: A Verse-Slate from Hushwatch
description: A slate propped against the middle Hushwatch stone, chalked in a hand the Wardens do not know: 'Say one name and turn for home; / say ours, and you will not walk alone.'

name: A Verse-Slate from the Cliff Graves
description: A slate laid face down on the turned headstone at the Cliff Graves. The verse on it is in a child's hand: 'We did not stop. We went on singing / where nobody was listening.'
